title: Pick your style and markets
desc: Choose a trading style that fits your time, and a short list of markets

cards.title: Which style fits you?
cards.situation: You work 9 to 5. You have 30 minutes each evening to look at charts. Which trading style fits your time?

options.text: Day trading: in and out the same day
options.feedback: Day trading looks exciting, but it needs you at the screen during work hours. You can’t give it that time.

options.text: Swing trading: holds for days to weeks
options.feedback: Swing trades can be checked once a day, after the close. That fits your evenings.

options.text: Quick trades on your lunch break
options.feedback: Lunch-break trades are rushed day trades. You can’t watch them once you’re back at work.

cards.work: Day trading needs hours at the screen while the market is open. You have 30 minutes after it closes.

cards.title: Pick a style that fits your clock
cards.text: Your **[[trading-style|style]]** is how long you hold a trade. Pick the one that fits the time you really have, not the one that looks most exciting.

visual.label: Three trading styles: how long each holds a trade and how often you check it

cards.title: A few markets, known well
cards.text: Forty markets means you know none of them well. Four means you learn how each one moves.

items.label: 4 markets
items.text: US index fund · Big tech stock · Big bank stock · Gold

cards.foot: For each market you learn its normal daily move, its busy hours and its big news dates, like earnings.

cards.title: Once a week
cards.q: You can only look at the market on Sunday evenings. You want to hold for weeks or months. Which style fits?

options.feedback: Day trading needs hours at the screen while markets are open. One look a week can’t cover that.
Swing trades often need a look every day. One check a week, holding for months, is position trading.
Position trades last weeks to months and need a look about once a week. That fits your Sunday evenings.
Style matters: it has to fit the time you really have. One look a week fits only the slowest style.

cards.title: A starter list
cards.q: Which list of markets is the better start for a beginner?

options.text: Every market on the app, so you never miss a move
options.feedback: Watching everything means knowing nothing well. A short list lets you learn how each market really moves.

options.text: 4 or 5 markets you follow and understand
options.feedback: A short list lets you learn each market’s normal daily move, busy hours and news dates.
What’s trending changes every day. You’d never learn how any one market really moves.

options.text: Only the markets that moved most this week
options.feedback: Last week’s biggest movers change every week. You’d never learn how any one market really moves.

cards.headline: Your style fits your clock.
lines: Pick the style that fits the time you really have.
Day trading needs hours at the screen while markets are open.
Start with a few markets you understand.
